chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi informed me, saying: Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Maliki narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Salt al-Hirawi narrated to us, saying: al-Ridha Ali ibn Musa, peace be upon them both, narrated to us, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali the Martyr, from his father the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon them all, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said:
"Faith is a statement to be uttered, a deed to be acted upon, and an acknowledgement by intellectual recognition."
Abu al-Salt said: I related this hadith in a gathering of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Ahmad said to me: "O Abu al-Salt! If this chain of narration were read over the insane, they would recover."

key_terms.الإسناد: Isnad -- chain of narration through which hadith is transmitted
key_terms.الإيمان: Iman (faith) -- comprehensive belief encompassing speech, action, and knowledge
key_terms.عرفان العقول: Intellectual recognition -- cognitive understanding and conviction
key_terms.عمل معمول: A deed acted upon -- practical implementation of faith
key_terms.قول مقول: A statement uttered -- verbal profession of faith (shahada)

ai.seo_question: What are the three components of faith (iman) according to Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) defined faith (iman) as comprising three inseparable components: verbal profession (qawl), practical action (amal), and intellectual conviction (irfan al-uqul). This hadith is transmitted through the famous "golden chain" (silsilat al-dhahab) -- from Imam al-Ridha through all seven preceding Imams back to the Prophet. Ahmad ibn Hanbal's remark about the chain's healing power underscores the extraordinary reverence even Sunni scholars held for this unbroken Alid chain of transmission.
